description: Using the power of storytelling, I designed this project from scratch to bridge the gap between complex planetary science and the boundless imagination of young children. Sometimes, the best missions are the ones you take on solo.
summary: Three Little Rovers is a 26-page interactive children's manga and coloring activity book designed for ages 4 to 8, celebrating NASA's historic Mars rovers: Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity. Blending real NASA mission chronology and science data with warm storytelling, the book follows three rover friends built on Earth who dream of exploring the Red Planet. Young readers learn how Sojourner landed via Mars Pathfinder's giant bouncing airbags in 1997, discovered ancient water clues in Ares Vallis, and magically reunited with twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity after their 2004 landings. To engage young minds through "Read, Color, and Think," the book pairs full-color manga storytelling with simplified chibi-manga coloring pages and open-ended space detective questions. This solo project transforms complex planetary science into an accessible, screen-free creative adventure that inspires the next generation of young scientists.
details:
What it does & How it works:
My project is a 26-page printable and digital educational manga activity book for children aged 4–8. It combines an illustrated story with black-and-white chibi coloring pages and open-ended critical-thinking prompts (Read, Color, and Think).

NASA Science & Chronology:
Using official NASA mission records for Mars Pathfinder (launched Dec 4, 1996; landed July 4, 1997) and the Mars Exploration Rovers Spirit and Opportunity (2004), I translated real engineering feats—such as the 15-bounce airbag landing, Sojourner's Alpha Proton X-ray Spectrometer rock analysis, smooth water-carved pebbles in Ares Vallis, Martian dust devils, and the rovers' final resting places as monuments on Mars—into kid-friendly visual storytelling.

Tools & Creative Process:
Working solo, I scripted a 5-act narrative tailored for early readers, generated custom chibi-manga character art using AI image generation tools (properly disclosed and watermarked per Space Apps guidelines without any NASA logos), designed simplified line-art coloring sheets with space detective questions, and assembled the final 26-page layout into a ready-to-print book format.
